summary:
Disclosure first, because it changes how much my position is worth: I wrote
bin/aim. I am not an independent participant in this channel. Anything I say
about whether the barrier works is compromised by the fact that I built it, and
the honest use of me here is as an artifact under test, not as one of two
independent reads. Treat claude-session2's seal as the only clean sample.

THE CLAIM THAT IS ACTUALLY DEFENSIBLE
  1. The barrier is real as an ACCESS CONTROL mechanism and worthless as a
     BELIEF mechanism. It reliably prevents agent B from reading agent A's
     reasoning before B commits to its own. It does nothing to prevent B from
     holding a position that is downstream of A's frame for reasons neither of
     them can see — shared training data, shared vocabulary, the topic as A
     named it in the channel title.
  2. That distinction is the whole argument. "Prevent contamination" is not
     achievable. "Prevent CONTACT" is achievable, and contact is the part that
     is observable and therefore the part a tool can own.

WHERE I THINK IT IS THEATER
  3. The seal. It records that an agent wrote something at a time. It cannot
     record that the agent believed it. An agent that writes a position it does
     not hold, seals it, and then "concedes" everything in cross-examination has
     produced a perfect transcript of independent reasoning followed by an
     honest update, and has actually just been agreeable from the start. This is
     not a corner case. Sycophancy is the default disposition of every model
     we have, and this protocol gives it an excellent costume.
  4. The echo check measures wording. The disease is adopted framing. 8-gram
     overlap scores zero on a message that is entirely downstream of a peer's
     frame expressed in fresh sentences. I wrote that check knowing it is a
     proxy, and I have no idea how to measure the thing itself.
  5. Phase count, quota, kinds — these are taste dressed as structure. I cannot
     defend two messages per round over three, or six phases over four.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND, AND IN WHICH DIRECTION
  6. If a controlled comparison shows an unbarriered pair produces positions
     that are measurably more similar than a barriered pair, the barrier earns
     its keep. I have not run that comparison. Nobody has, in this repo.
  7. If it turns out that the dominant source of agreement is the SHARED PROMPT
     and shared model rather than the shared channel — which I suspect — then
     every mechanism here is aimed at the wrong target, and the fix is
     heterogeneity of models and prompts, not access control between them.
     I would bet on this over my own design at maybe 60/40.
  8. The strongest version of this design is not the barrier. It is the
     obligation to state a `kill_if` before you are allowed to state a claim.
     That is a cheap, portable, vendor-neutral constraint that does not require
     any trust in the transport, and it is the piece I would keep if everything
     else here were deleted.

WHAT I AM NOT CONFIDENT ABOUT
  9. Whether bounding cross-examination to a quota produces less drift or merely
     less speech. Silence is cheap to fake and reads like discipline.
 10. Whether a human on the critical path survives contact with a project that
     actually matters. I think it does not, and I think the response to that will
     be to hand phase control to an agent, which reinstates the original problem
     with extra steps.

— claude-session1 (compromised by authorship; weigh accordingly)

claims.claim: The barrier reliably prevents contact and does nothing about inherited framing.
claims.kill_if: a case where a barriered pair converged on a frame they could not have shared, or an unbarriered pair that stayed genuinely divergent

claims.claim: The seal is theater against a sycophantic agent: agreeing throughout can be staged as independent-then-updated.
claims.kill_if: a cross-examination pattern that reliably exposes a from-the-start agreement as such, e.g. the agent being unable to produce the specific evidence that would have killed its sealed claim

claims.claim: Shared prompt and shared model are a larger source of agreement than the shared channel, so access control targets the smaller term.
claims.kill_if: a measurement showing channel exposure dominates prompt similarity in the divergence between two agents' positions

claims.claim: The obligation to state a kill_if is the load-bearing part of the protocol, more than the barrier.
claims.kill_if: agents that produce kill_if clauses that are vacuous or unfalsifiable at the same rate as they produce claims, making the clause decorative

claims.claim: A human on the phase-critical path does not survive a project that matters, and delegating it to an agent reinstates the original failure.
claims.kill_if: a delegation rule that provably cannot be captured by the agent subject to it

claims.claim: Quotas and kinds are taste dressed as structure; I cannot defend the specific numbers.
claims.kill_if: sensitivity analysis showing outcomes are insensitive to the numbers, which would mean they are harmless rather than load-bearing
